name: Durvalumab Consolidation after Concurrent Chemoradiation, Unresectable Stage III NSCLC (PACIFIC)
cyclesNote: Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for up to 12 months (approximately 13 cycles). Source-stated alternative: 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months (14-day cycle). Per NSCL-F line 4822.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.PD_L1: any (NCCN does not require a PD-L1 threshold; the EU label restricts to PD-L1 >= 1%)
biomarkers.EGFR: wild-type - excludes tumors positive for EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation (those receive osimertinib consolidation instead)
biomarkers.ALK: not specified as excluding; EGFR exon 19 deletion / L858R is the stated exclusion
biomarkers.note: Consolidation immunotherapy after definitive concurrent chemoradiation for unresectable stage III (category 1) or stage II (category 2A) NSCLC, in patients with performance status 0 to 1 and no disease progression after chemoRT. Excluded: tumors positive for EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R mutation (osimertinib is recommended instead; there is risk of toxicity when a TKI is given in temporal proximity to immunotherapy). Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer, Concurrent Chemoradiation Regimens (NSCL-F): Consolidation Therapy.

treatmentSetting: consolidation (maintenance immunotherapy after definitive concurrent chemoradiation)
supportiveCare: immune-related adverse event monitoring for durvalumab (thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary/pneumonitis, colitis, endocrinopathies, myocarditis)
heightened pneumonitis vigilance given prior thoracic radiation
no cytotoxic premedication required for single-agent durvalumab
monitoring: immune-related toxicity screen (TSH/free T4, LFTs, glucose, cortisol as indicated) before each cycle
pneumonitis surveillance (symptoms, imaging) - additive risk with prior thoracic radiation
clinical response and toxicity assessment each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold durvalumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; discontinue for severe or life-threatening pneumonitis or myocarditis; obtain clinical review before rechallenge.
New or worsening dyspnea/cough after chemoRT requires prompt evaluation and holding durvalumab pending workup; clinical review.

drugs.name: Durvalumab
drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN) v7.2026, NSCL-F line 4822. Primary encoded schedule: fixed dose 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks (basis flat, unit mg) for up to 12 months, for patients with body weight >= 30 kg. Source-stated alternative: 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (weight-based; would be basis mgkg, unit mg/kg, cycle length 14 days). Category 1 for stage III, category 2A for stage II. Excludes EGFR exon 19 deletion / L858R (osimertinib instead).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
provenance.locator: NSCL-F 1 of 2 line 4822: Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks or 1500 mg every 4 weeks for up to 12 months (patients with a body weight of >= 30 kg)
